description: Spanish vocabulary register audit list. 'formal' = literary/legal/report-language item dead or stiff in conversation; 'preferred' = what Spanish speakers actually say. Deck targets neutral Latin American Spanish (tú/usted, ustedes; no vos, no vosotros). Severity: 'high' = dead in speech, swap wherever it appears in conversational cards; 'medium' = written-leaning, swap in beginner content. See docs/spanish-register-policy.md.

dead_in_speech.rationale: Literary and legal constructions no Spanish speaker uses in conversation anywhere in the Spanish-speaking world.

entries.note: The accentless conjunction mas (= but) is purely literary. más (more) is a different word — exempt.
«el señor cuyo coche está afuera» → «el señor que tiene el coche afuera». Alive in writing, dead in conversation.
Legal fossil («si hubiere lugar»). Survives only in law and fixed sayings («sea lo que fuere» → «sea lo que sea»).
Report/minutes language; conversation uses también or además.
Only the legalese determiner sense («dicha persona» → «esa persona»). Participle of decir («ha dicho») is everyday — exempt.
